title: Simulated crew scenario: 4 fictional crewmembers, MET days 368-412 (seeded, labelled)

source.name: LANDFALL seeded crew scenario, seed 20261114 (ingest/sim_crew.py)
source.license: Apache-2.0 (LANDFALL). Replayed inputs keep their publishers' terms; see their snapshots.
source.citation: LANDFALL simulated crew scenario (seed 20261114), ingest/sim_crew.py, https://github.com/amaroguilherme/landfall. Calibrated against Barger et al. 2014 (PMID 25127232) and Basner et al. 2011 (PMID 22025811); SPE shape from NOAA NCEI GOES-07 EPS (October 1989); Mars-surface baseline from NASA CCMC iSWA MSL RAD; conjunction window from JPL Horizons when present.

caveats: SIMULATED SCENARIO - NOT CREW DATA. Continuous crew vitals are simulated because no public time series of real crew wearable data exists. Every crew value is produced by a seeded generator (seed 20261114; ingest/_sim_model.py) and is identical on every re-run.

Calibration sources: Barger et al. 2014, Lancet Neurol (ISS actigraphic sleep 6.09 h per night; 12 of 16 ISS crew used sleep-promoting drugs) for sleep duration; Basner, Mollicone & Dinges 2011, Acta Astronaut (PVT-B lapse = RT >= 355 ms) for the lapse definition; the CSA Bio-Monitor / Hexoskin Astroskin channel cadences (300-s HRV windows, 1-Hz skin temperature) for the band summaries, as recorded in the project plan from the product's datatype registry (not re-verified by this generator); SPEC section 7 for the episode script. Everything else is a design choice, listed per variable in data.variables[*].calibration.
CM-1..CM-4 are fictional: no names, no real PII. Mood is simulated for everyone, private by default and never alerts.

Episodes are scripted, not discovered: on their robust days (data.self_check.episodes) episode values sit at least 6 baseline SDs from the crewmember's baseline mean (|t| >= 5.8 on Tier B's single-case test, critical 4.221 at df 13). CM-1's two PVT-B indicators ramp up first, 2 to 6 baseline SDs out on days 404-406 (day 406 already crosses the critical value). Non-episode days are drawn within 1.4 baseline SDs (|t| <= 1.35), so no unscripted reliable change appears. Real data would also produce chance reliable changes: about alpha = 0.001 per indicator-day only if day-to-day noise were normal and independent, and more with the autocorrelated, skewed noise of real days (engine/rules/personal.json rci.caveat). Real day-to-day variability is also larger than the deliberately low SDs used here.
Daily values are stamped when their measurement window closes, so 'now' (MET 0412/14:20:00) has no 24-h urine, fluid or daytime-light value for day 412 yet: that day is incomplete.
career_effective_dose is a design-choice prior (mSv), not a calculation. The SPE day's absorbed dose rate (uGy/day) is never converted to effective dose: LANDFALL makes no personal dose projection.

SPE day: the event TIME PROFILE is REAL (NOAA NCEI GOES-7 >10 MeV proton flux, October 1989, read from swpc_spe_replay) and only time-shifted, so its first S3-level sample lands at MET 0412/14:15:00. vehicle.series.proton_flux_10mev carries that replayed flux unchanged as the habitat proton-monitor reading; vehicle.series.onboard_dose_rate is the same profile under an assumed flux-to-dose scaling. GOES measured in Earth orbit: using its flux as the reading at a Mars habitat (no distance, shielding or atmospheric correction) is a scenario assumption.

SPE day: the quiet-time baseline is REAL: the median MSL RAD 'dose_e_total' dose rate, 184.73 uGy/day, read from hapi_msl_rad_dose. The flux-to-dose scaling (S3 flux = 10x baseline) is an ASSUMPTION standing in for shielding, distance and atmospheric transport, not a radiation-transport calculation.

Calendar: MET day 412 is mapped into a REAL Mars solar-conjunction window taken from horizons_mars_comms (2028-03-12T12:00:00Z to 2028-03-29T23:00:00Z); the mission, its launch date (MET epoch) and the pairing with the 1989 event are fictional.

generator.rng: random.Random(f'{seed}:{stream}') per crewmember x variable; random() and gauss() only

met.convention: MET = integer seconds since MET epoch; day = floor(MET / 86400), so MET day 412 starts at 35,596,800 s

record.min_elongation_basis: smallest of the daily 00:00 UTC samples (not a refined minimum)
record.basis: derived: Sun-Earth-Mars elongation below the calibrated threshold (edges linearly interpolated between daily samples, rounded to the hour)

calendar.selection: first real window starting on/after 2026-11-14 that is >= 10 d 06 h long (else the latest long-enough one, else the longest); now = window stop - 11 d 06 h (window long enough)

source.arithmetic: linear interpolation between the daily 00:00 UTC rows around now_utc

input.title: Earth-Mars light time and solar conjunction windows, 2026-2029 (JPL Horizons)
input.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics Group

observation_format.expand: for each series: observation = {crew_id, variable, value: v[i], unit, t: t[i] (or start_t + i*step_s), source, provenance: 'simulated'}; vehicle series have crew_id null
observation_format.t_meaning: MET seconds when the value became available (end of its measurement window)
observation_format.missing: null = no sample (a gap to show as stale/missing per [V2 10020]); never zero

sleep_duration.label: Sleep duration (actigraphy)
sleep_duration.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
sleep_duration.definition: Total sleep time of the main sleep episode ending on that MET day, from band actigraphy.

source.citation: Barger LK, Flynn-Evans EE, Kubey A, Walsh L, Ronda JM, Wang W, Wright KP Jr, Czeisler CA. Prevalence of sleep deficiency and use of hypnotic drugs in astronauts before, during, and after spaceflight: an observational study. Lancet Neurol 2014;13(9):904-912. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(14)70122-X. PMID 25127232
source.note: ISS crew obtained 6.09 h (SD 0.67) of actigraphic sleep per night in flight.

source.rationale: Pre-shift schedule: sleep period 22:00-06:00 MET clock (midpoint 02:00). Day-to-day SDs are set deliberately low so the scripted episodes are unambiguous; real within-person variability is larger, which is why Tier B prints its false-alarm rate.

calibration.item: CM-1 after the day-403 schedule shift

source.rationale: Scripted short sleep opportunity; same order as the 4-h time-in-bed partial sleep deprivation protocol used to validate the PVT-B (Basner 2011).

sleep_midpoint_shift.label: Sleep midpoint shift
sleep_midpoint_shift.definition: Midpoint of the main sleep episode minus 02:00 MET, the midpoint of the pre-shift scheduled sleep period (22:00-06:00). Positive = later.

source.rationale: Pre-shift schedule: sleep period 22:00-06:00 MET clock (midpoint 02:00). Day-to-day SDs are set deliberately low so the scripted episodes are unambiguous; real within-person variability is larger, which is why Tier B prints its false-alarm rate.

Pre-shift schedule: sleep period 22:00-06:00 MET clock (midpoint 02:00). Day-to-day SDs are set deliberately low so the scripted episodes are unambiguous; real within-person variability is larger, which is why Tier B prints its false-alarm rate.
Partial adaptation to a 3-h later schedule (the circadian system lags the schedule).

pvt_lapses.label: PVT-B lapses
pvt_lapses.definition: Number of responses with reaction time >= 355 ms on the 3-min PVT-B.

source.citation: Basner M, Mollicone D, Dinges DF. Validity and sensitivity of a brief psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B) to total and partial sleep deprivation. Acta Astronaut 2011;69(11-12):949-959. doi:10.1016/j.actaastro.2011.07.015. PMID 22025811
source.note: The paper lowers the PVT-B lapse threshold from 500 ms to 355 ms. No NASA standard adopts 355 ms; it is attributed to the paper only.

source.rationale: Plausible rested values; not fitted.
Scripted to sit at least 6 baseline SDs above the baseline mean from day 407 (|t| >= 5.8 on Tier B's single-case test; critical 4.221).

pvt_median_rt.label: PVT-B median reaction time
pvt_median_rt.definition: Median reaction time of the 3-min PVT-B, in ms.

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted.

calibration.value: 262-281 ms on days 404-406, 296-304 ms from day 407

source.rationale: Scripted slowing that accompanies the lapse increase.

light_exposure_daytime.label: Daytime light exposure
light_exposure_daytime.cadence: daily (wake period, stamped at the next sleep onset)
light_exposure_daytime.definition: Mean photopic illuminance over the wake period, from the band light sensor.

source.rationale: No verified habitat illuminance value was used; kept unchanged through the episodes so it never fires on its own.

resting_hr.label: Resting heart rate
resting_hr.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
resting_hr.definition: Mean heart rate over the main sleep episode, from band ECG R-R intervals.

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted.

hrv_sdnn.label: HRV (SDNN)
hrv_sdnn.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
hrv_sdnn.definition: Median of the 300-s SDNN windows during the main sleep episode.

source.rationale: Mirrors the 300-s HRV cadence of the CSA Bio-Monitor (Hexoskin Astroskin) noted in the project plan; that datatype registry was not re-read by this generator.
Plausible values; not fitted.

skin_temp.label: Skin temperature
skin_temp.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
skin_temp.definition: Mean skin temperature over the main sleep episode, from the band (1 Hz channel).

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted. 1 Hz mirrors the Bio-Monitor skin-temperature channel noted in the project plan (not re-read here).

urine_volume_24h.label: 24-h urine output
urine_volume_24h.cadence: daily (MET-midnight to MET-midnight collection, stamped at its end)
urine_volume_24h.definition: Volume of the 24-h urine collection for that MET day, entered manually.

calibration.value: outside below 1,500 mL/day; approaching below 2,500 mL/day

source.rationale: The levels are owned and sourced by rule target_urine_output_24h in engine/rules/thresholds.json (NASA HRP Evidence Report, Risk of Renal Stone Formation); the generator only places values clearly on either side of them.

calibration.value: 2,780-2,900 mL (SD 100-105); every non-episode day of every crewmember stays above 2,500 mL

source.rationale: Crew meeting the 2.5-3 L/day hydration countermeasure target, so the rule's approach level never fires outside the episode; day-to-day SD deliberately low (about 4%).
Below the 1,500 mL/day level on every episode day and at least 6 baseline SDs below the baseline mean (|t| >= 5.8 on Tier B's single-case test; critical 4.221).

fluid_intake_24h.label: 24-h fluid intake
fluid_intake_24h.cadence: daily (same window as the urine collection)
fluid_intake_24h.definition: Logged fluid intake for that MET day.

source.rationale: Plausible values, about 0.55 L above urine output; not fitted.
Intake falls with output, as SPEC section 7 describes.

mood.label: Mood (self-report)
mood.cadence: daily at the 12:00 MET check-in (Noon Sight)
mood.definition: Self-rated mood, integer 1-5. PRIVATE by default and NON-ALERTING (SPEC 3.3, 7).

calibration.value: mostly 3-4; CM-1 dips to 2-3 during the sleep episode

source.rationale: Never alerts; excluded from the ground packet unless the crewmember consents.

vo2max.label: VO2max (periodic fitness test)
vo2max.definition: Aerobic capacity from the periodic in-flight fitness test.

source.rationale: Set by SPEC section 7 for the FFD demo: within the [V1 4001] microgravity-EVA floor (32.9) and outside the [V1 4002] surface-EVA floor (36.5). The floors themselves live in thresholds.json.
Comfortably above both floors so only CM-2 flips with the environment selector.

career_effective_dose.label: Career effective dose to date (prior)
career_effective_dose.cadence: one value per crewmember, at MET 0412/00:00
career_effective_dose.definition: Career effective dose to date before the SPE day, as it would come from the dosimetry record.

source.rationale: Not computed from any transport model. Chosen below 480 mSv (80% of the [V1 4030] 600 mSv limit) so the SPE case is driven by the onboard dose RATE ([V2 6164]), not by the career limit. The SPE day's absorbed dose is NOT added: LANDFALL does not convert uGy to mSv.

heart_rate.label: Heart rate (1-min)
heart_rate.cadence: PT1M, MET day 412 only, 00:00 to now
heart_rate.definition: 1-min mean heart rate from the band ECG.

source.rationale: Plausible values; the sleep segment is centred on that night's resting_hr.

cabin_ppco2.label: Cabin ppCO2 (1-h mean)
cabin_ppco2.definition: 1-hour mean cabin CO2 partial pressure; value k covers [start + k h, start + (k+1) h).

source.rationale: Kept below the 2.4 mmHg approach level of rule pel_cabin_ppco2_1h in engine/rules/thresholds.json (and the [V2 6004] 1-h mean limit of 3 mmHg) so it never competes with the scripted cases.

onboard_dose_rate.label: Onboard radiation monitor dose rate
onboard_dose_rate.definition: Absorbed dose rate reported by the habitat radiation monitor ([V2 6164] system), in the same unit as MSL RAD. Absorbed dose (Gy) is not effective dose (Sv).

source.arithmetic: median of MSL RAD 'dose_e_total' over the snapshot window; noise SD = (p95 - p05) / (2 x 1.6449)

calibration.value: NOAA NCEI GOES-7 >10 MeV flux, 19-21 Oct 1989, native 5-min samples

source.rationale: Stand-in for shielding, heliocentric distance and atmospheric transport, which LANDFALL does not model: the NOAA S3 flux level is mapped to 10x the measured Mars-surface quiet rate. Not a radiation-transport calculation; no effective dose (mSv) is derived from it.

source.rationale: Scenario assumption: no heliocentric-distance, shielding or atmospheric correction is applied. A real monitor at Mars would read a different (for a surface habitat, attenuated) flux.

source.arithmetic: median of MSL RAD 'dose_e_total' over the snapshot window; noise SD = (p95 - p05) / (2 x 1.6449)

mapping.rule: time shift only: the first replay sample >= 1,000 pfu (NOAA S3 level) is placed at MET 0412/14:15:00, 5 min before 'now'; sample order and spacing are untouched
mapping.pre_event_flux_method: median of the 12 h of replay samples before the SESC onset

scaling.formula: dose_rate(t) = RAD_baseline + noise + k * max(F(t) - F_pre, 0), k = (10 - 1) * RAD_baseline / (1000 pfu - F_pre)

source.rationale: Stand-in for shielding, heliocentric distance and atmospheric transport, which LANDFALL does not model: the NOAA S3 flux level is mapped to 10x the measured Mars-surface quiet rate. Not a radiation-transport calculation; no effective dose (mSv) is derived from it.

spe_day.note: At Mars no NOAA alert reaches the crew (noaa_scale_available false). The habitat proton monitor reading (vehicle.series.proton_flux_10mev) is the time-shifted Earth-orbit replay with no distance, shielding or atmospheric correction (a scenario assumption); applying NOAA's S3 level to it is a design choice of engine/rules/thresholds.json. onboard_dose_rate is the same profile under the assumed flux-to-dose scaling; source_flux_pfu repeats the flux beside each dose sample for auditing.

episodes.summary: 24-h urine output falls below 1,500 mL/day (the limit of rule target_urine_output_24h in engine/rules/thresholds.json) on MET days 398-401 while fluid intake falls as well; both recover from day 402. Every other urine value of every crewmember stays above the rule's 2,500 mL/day approach level.

On MET day 403 CM-1's work schedule shifts 3 h later and the sleep opportunity is shortened (vehicle-operations support). From the night ending on day 404 sleep shortens and its midpoint moves later; PVT-B lapses and median RT climb to at least 6 baseline SDs above the baseline mean by day 407 (|t| >= 5.8 on Tier B's single-case test, critical 4.221). The episode is still running at 'now' (no countermeasure is applied in the data, so the case can be acted on in the demo).

ffd_demo.expect: within the microgravity-EVA floor (32.9, [V1 4001]); outside the surface-EVA floor (36.5, [V1 4002])

self_check.method: SPEC section 5 single-case t (Crawford & Howell 1998): t = (x - mean) / (sd * sqrt(1 + 1/n)), sd = sample SD (n-1), df = n - 1; reliable when |t| > the two-tailed critical value at alpha 0.001 (4.221 at df 13). z = |x - mean| / sd is the same distance in baseline SDs
